summary: Clyde River Airport (YCY) is a small regional airport serving the Inuit hamlet of Clyde River (Kangiqtugaapik) on the eastern coast of Baffin Island in Nunavut, Canada. Located just north of the Arctic Circle at approximately 70.5°N latitude, it functions as a vital lifeline for one of Canada's most remote communities, with no road access to the outside world. The airport primarily handles turboprop aircraft serving scheduled passenger routes and charter flights.
faqs:
Q: What airlines serve Clyde River Airport?
A: Canadian North operates scheduled passenger flights connecting Clyde River to Iqaluit and other Baffin Island communities, typically using turboprop aircraft such as the ATR 42.

Q: Is there road access to Clyde River?
A: No, Clyde River is a fly-in community with no road connections to other settlements. Air travel is the primary means of transportation in and out.

Q: What facilities are available at the airport?
A: The terminal offers basic amenities appropriate for a small remote airport. Travelers should expect limited services and prepare accordingly.

Q: When is the best time to visit Clyde River?
A: Summer months (June through August) offer milder temperatures and nearly 24-hour daylight, while winter (February to April) is ideal for viewing the Northern Lights.
transport_tips: Since Clyde River has no road access, travelers must rely on the airport for arrival and departure. Taxis and ATVs are typically used for the short transfer between the airport and the hamlet. Booking flights well in advance is recommended, as weather-related delays and cancellations are common in the Arctic.
local_tip: Bring extra layers even in summer—temperatures can drop quickly near the coast, and the terminal building may be cool. Local contacts often advise packing a thermos with a hot drink for any potential waits, as services are minimal and weather delays can extend waiting times.
